title: Man. Post. Cap. IX: PLAC second reason — εἰς τὸν κόσμον = all humans
pass_a_gloss: Second reason: the next words—εἰς τὸν κόσμον εἰσῆλθε, entered into the world. You and nearly all interpreters grant 'world' = all humans; no proof needed. So: the sin that entered through Adam into all is not Adam's actual but hereditary corruption; Paul speaks of that entered-sin; therefore not of Adam's actual but of hereditary corruption.
pass_b_english: A second reason the following words supply me, eis ton kosmon eiselthe, entered into the world. But that by the world all humans are understood, since you and almost all interpreters confess it, there is no need to prove. I reason therefore thus: The sin which entered through Adam into all humans is not Adam's actual sin, but hereditary corruption. But the Apostle speaks of the sin which entered through Adam into all humans. Therefore he speaks not of Adam's actual sin, but of hereditary corruption.
source_text: Secundam rationem mihi suppeditant verba sequentia, εἰς τὸν κόσμον εἰσῆλθε in mundum introiit. Per mundum autem omnes homines intelligi cum tu & fere omnes interpretes fateamini, nihil opus est probare. Sic igitur ratiocinor, Peccatum, quod per Adamum in omnes homines introiit, non est peccatum actuale Adami, sed corruptio haereditaria. Atqui Apostolus loquitur de peccato quod per Adamum in omnes homines introiit. Ergo loquitur non de peccato actuali Adami, sed de corruptione haereditaria.

choices.choice: Entered-sin into all = hereditary, not actual
